category_title: Students in vocational settings who struggle with professional norms like punctuality
student_description: This student has a history of friction with mainstream schooling, often exhibiting non-compliant behaviors like lateness, loud disruptions, and ignoring routines. They reject traditional, authority-based school discipline, which only worsens their resistance. They uniquely require a vocational approach where all routines, corrections, and tasks are explicitly framed around real-world workplace expectations rather than classroom compliance.

criteria.rationale: The student struggles with standard school routines but responds well when daily procedures are treated as vocational training.
criteria.check: The long-term plan establishes daily administrative routines (such as signing in and out) as explicit workplace practices rather than school compliance tasks.

criteria.rationale: Long contact hours lead to lost focus, requiring a shift from traditional academic study to varied, role-based vocational tasks.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates extended professional role-plays interspersed with diverse, practical, hands-on activities (e.g., mock interviews, research) to maintain engagement.
